verdict.rationale: E2B markets itself as providing 'secure isolated sandboxes in the cloud' for running AI-generated code (e2b-gh-3), and its self-hosted infra runs on separate Terraform-provisioned infrastructure (e2b-gh-2) with configurable network egress controls (e2b-docs-10), implying host separation. However, no evidence explicitly addresses how host secrets/credentials are kept unreachable (e.g., no mention of VM-level isolation mechanism, secret injection safeguards, or credential-scoping), and there's no independent security audit or hands-on test confirming this boundary holds. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of the isolation mechanism (e.g., microVM/hypervisor boundary) preventing host secret access, and independent verification (pentest, audit, or community confirmation) that credentials are unreachable from sandboxed code.
